answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a graduated work-history bond. A new agent starts on a narrow mesa of permissions: it may only take small, verifiable jobs whose outputs are checked against a crystal-clear specification by randomly assigned peers. Each completed job adds earned credit, while a failed or copied result burns credit and flags the identity. A gale of fresh accounts cannot flood the market, because every identity must slowly climb the same ladder of proven work before touching high-value transactions, and climbing costs more than one fake account can gain.
